lines: Jamie Alvarez
+1 (555) 010-5820 | jamie.alvarez@example.com | example.com/in/jalvarez
EDUCATION
Riverbend Polytechnic | B.S. in Industrial Engineering | Metro City, USA | Sep 2014 - May 2018
EXPERIENCE
Greenleaf Florist | Delivery Driver and Shop Assistant | Metro City, USA | Sep 2025 - Present
- Delivered 30 to 40 arrangements a day across the city and took cash and card payments at the door.
- Prepared weekend wedding orders with the head florist and kept the cooler stocked and labeled.
Lakeview Distribution | Operations Analyst | Metro City, USA | Jul 2018 - Jan 2021
- Raised forecast accuracy from 70% to 85% by switching the MAPE calculation to cover only SKUs that sold every week.
- Ran a time study of the returns desk; my findings led to a triage station that cut returns processing time from 3 days to 1.
- Wrote the dock scheduling rules for 12 carriers, cutting average trailer wait at the dock from 95 to 40 minutes.
- Set up cycle counting for the 2,000 highest-value locations, raising inventory record accuracy from 91% to 98.5% within a year.
Crestway Foods | Supply Chain Planner | Metro City, USA | Feb 2021 - Jul 2025
- Rebuilt weekly demand planning for 1,400 SKUs across 3 distribution centers with a seasonal forecast model, cutting stockouts from 6.2% to 2.8% while inventory fell by $1.9M.
- Cut inbound freight cost per pallet from $48 to $41 over two quarters by consolidating supplier pickups into four regional milk runs.
- Set reorder points for every SKU from 18 months of daily demand and supplier lead-time data, reviewed monthly with the category managers.

- Scoring 40 vendors weekly on on-time delivery, fill rate, lead-time variance and invoice accuracy, and sharing the scorecards with buyers before each quarterly review, raised on-time inbound deliveries from 81% to 93%.
- Raised the packaging line's overall equipment effectiveness (OEE) from 71% to 112% by cutting changeover time and micro-stops.
- Trained 6 planners on the new forecasting workflow and wrote its exception-handling guide, which the team still uses for promotions.
PROJECTS
Last-Mile Routing Study | Independent Project | Python | Oct 2024 - Present
- Modeled a regional grocer's 85 daily delivery stops as a vehicle-routing problem, cutting planned route miles 18% against the grocer's current routes.
- Cut average route length from 120 to 90 miles, a 40% reduction, by solving the routing problem with customer time windows.
- Raised on-time deliveries by 9% in simulation, from 84% to 93%, by adding customer time windows to the routing model.
Regional Food Bank Warehouse | Volunteer Consultant, Team of 4 | Excel | Mar 2022 - Jul 2022
- Analyzed warehouse operations and made recommendations to the food bank's leadership.
- The donation intake process was mapped and two duplicate data-entry steps were removed, so donations reached the shelves a day sooner.
- Wrote a slotting guide that the volunteer coordinators used to re-slot the warehouse again after its spring expansion.
SKILLS
Tools: Excel, Python
Methods: demand forecasting, inventory planning, time studies, vehicle routing

items.says: The move from Supply Chain Planner to Delivery Driver and Shop Assistant is unexplained.
items.because: Without context, a recruiter may question the transition instead of focusing on seven years of relevant experience.

items.says: Experience is not ordered newest first.
items.because: Lakeview appears above the later Crestway role, hiding the progression and forcing readers to reconstruct the chronology.

items.says: The Greenleaf role receives too much visual weight relative to the operations and supply-chain roles.
items.because: Two bullets make it appear equally important and can distract from the intended career narrative.

items.says: Leading with the 2018 degree understates the more recent professional record.
items.because: Opening with education delays the strongest evidence of current capability.

items.says: “Delivered” and “took” use past tense for a current role.
The delivery workload figure has no result for timeliness or accuracy.
items.because: It shows volume handled but not whether deliveries were completed reliably.

items.says: “Prepared” and “kept” use past tense for a current role.
“Prepared weekend wedding orders” does not identify the candidate’s specific tasks.
items.because: The ambiguity hides the level of responsibility in the shop.

items.says: “Kept the cooler stocked and labeled” does not show its effect.
items.because: Without a connection to readiness, accuracy, or freshness, it reads as routine maintenance.

items.says: “Raised forecast accuracy from 70% to 85%” presents a change in the evaluated SKU population as a forecasting improvement.
items.because: Excluding harder-to-forecast SKUs can mechanically improve the metric, making the figures incomparable unless they use the same population.

items.says: “MAPE” is unexplained jargon on its first use.
“From 3 days to 1” omits the unit after the second number.
items.because: The comparison is grammatically incomplete even though the reader can infer the unit.

items.says: “My findings led to” uses a personal pronoun and indirectly attributes the outcome.
“Dock scheduling rules” does not identify what changed in carrier scheduling.
“Set up cycle counting” does not show how the program was structured or controlled.
“A seasonal forecast model” does not identify the technique or treatment of seasonality.
Setting reorder points has no resulting change in service, inventory, or replenishment performance.
items.because: Without an outcome, it can read as routine parameter maintenance rather than a planning improvement.

items.says: “Reviewed monthly with the category managers” does not clearly identify what was reviewed or who reviewed it.
The on-time delivery result is buried after a long method-led opening.
items.because: A scanning reader may register scorecard administration without reaching the improvement.

items.says: The gerund opening does not give an ended role a direct past-tense action.
An OEE increase from 71% to 112% is impossible under the standard definition.
items.because: OEE is the product of components each capped at 100%, so it cannot exceed 100%.

items.says: “By cutting changeover time and micro-stops” does not explain how the reductions were achieved.
items.because: It hides the process-improvement technique and what the candidate personally changed.

items.says: The team’s continued use of the guide shows adoption but not its benefit.
“Cutting planned route miles 18% against” is grammatically incorrect.
items.because: It omits “by” and uses “against” awkwardly, making the result harder to read.

items.says: The vehicle-routing formulation does not say how optimized routes were produced.
items.because: A technical reader cannot tell whether the project used a solver, heuristic, or another approach.

items.says: The 18% mileage result is less visible than the method-led opening.
items.because: A scanning recruiter reaches the setup before discovering the main result.

items.says: Calling a decrease from 120 to 90 miles a 40% reduction is arithmetically wrong.
items.because: The decrease is 30 miles, or 25% of the original 120 miles.

items.says: Customer time windows name a constraint, not the optimization method.
items.because: A technical reader cannot assess how the problem was solved or reproduced.

items.says: “By 9%” confuses percent with percentage points.
items.because: An increase from 84% to 93% is 9 percentage points, or approximately 10.7% relative.

items.says: Adding customer time windows does not explain their technical implementation.
items.because: The reader cannot tell how the constraint was represented or enforced in the model.

items.says: The routing project reports the route-mileage achievement twice with conflicting reductions of 18% and 40%.
items.because: Readers cannot tell whether the bullets describe different scenarios, and the inconsistency weakens confidence in the calculations.

items.says: “Made recommendations” does not show what was adopted or improved.
items.because: Advice alone does not demonstrate that the analysis influenced an operational decision.

items.says: “Analyzed warehouse operations” is too broad to show what was examined or how Excel supported the analysis.
“Made recommendations to” is weaker and less direct than a single action verb.
The strongest result is not the entry’s opening bullet.
items.because: Moving this specific process change and measured benefit first would give a scanning reader immediate evidence of impact.

items.says: The mapping and removal of duplicate steps are written in passive voice.
items.because: The construction hides who performed the work.

items.says: “Wrote a slotting guide” does not show how locations were assigned or what analysis informed the guide.
“Re-slot the warehouse again” is redundant.
“That the volunteer coordinators used to” is unnecessarily wordy.
